title: Steal like a Year 11
question: Which habits from real companies, offices and startups should Keel steal, and what do they look like for six Year 11s with school, jobs, sport and families?
serves: North star 1 (a distinctive, human team voice) and the Final Report's Articulation criterion; every habit also has to make Keel's IPS help to Caplet better before Sat 7 Nov
essence: We read how twelve real companies work (Pixar, Toyota, Amazon, Netflix and eight more) and argued for four rounds about which habits six busy Year 11s should steal.

Nine passed. The big three: whoever owns a line decides it unless it can't be undone, and then all six vote once; anyone can type "CORD:" to flag a problem at any hour, and the first reply is "thanks"; boring jobs get dealt out on Sundays instead of waiting for a volunteer.

For Caplet: our help on the IPS now gets argued and checked before it reaches you, and the research we found on how teams decide well (some of it from Wharton itself) is yours to use in the Final Report.
decided: Doors: the owner decides anything she can fix in one lunch before 09:00 Sat 7 Nov; anything one-way (submitted, promised to Laura, the floor, the range, the shortfall plan) gets one vote of all six (6-0)
CORD: flag a problem any hour with CORD:, first reply "thanks", a wrong fact is a cord the same day (6-0)
UGLY: once a week, one-way IPS lines only, alone first then together (Girotra, Terwiesch and Ulrich, 2010); who picks is still open (5-1, Kai against)
Sealed: sums are re-run, never voted; judgement numbers get a sealed guess, reasons, a second sealed guess, and the median (6-0)
Budget: every question gets a price before it opens; all habits together cost at most 60 minutes a person a week (6-0)
The deal and the read-aloud: unclaimed jobs dealt round on Sundays; someone who isn't Tess reads the requirement list aloud against each draft (6-0)
Cold read: two readers who know no finance, three questions with right answers, never asked about numbers; Kai plays Spinnaker (6-0)
Log first: decision in the log before the chat, with the owner's why, the dissenter's name and what would change their mind (6-0)
Cool-down: nothing new assigned Mon 9 to Fri 13 Nov, except one owner reading the Final Report instructions (6-0)
Refused: Netflix's keeper test, Bridgewater's dot collector and taped meetings, six-page memos, a stop-everything switch
seeds: UGLY's pick: should a cold reader who never saw the pile choose among the top three lines, since makers and groups both pick badly? (chat vote by Wed 28 Oct, 9 p.m.)
Sealed guesses on a real number: run them on the IPS's confidence in the 2031 range before Sat 31 Oct and see if the six land somewhere different from Jun's model
If no CORD is pulled by Fri 6 Nov, the habits were decoration (Nora)
changes: keel/CULTURE.md: new section "We're six Year 11s, not a firm" with the nine habits, what was refused and why
